examples: I collect pretty rocks.
We collect shells at the beach.
The teacher collects our papers.

more.def: To gather things together, sometimes as a hobby.
examples: He collects stamps from countries all around the world.
A truck collects the trash every Tuesday.
Bees collect nectar from flowers to make honey.

easy.def: To move toward the one who is speaking.
examples: Come here, please.
The bus comes at eight.
My friend came to my house.

more.def: To move toward a person or place, or to arrive somewhere.
examples: Please come to the front of the class and show your drawing.
The mail carrier comes to our street every morning.
Our cousins came all the way from Texas for the holiday.
My bed is so comfortable.
This chair is comfortable.
I feel comfortable in my pajamas.

more.def: Feeling relaxed and at ease, or making you feel that way.
examples: These shoes are comfortable enough to wear all day.
She felt comfortable talking to her grandmother about anything.
The hotel room was small but comfortable.

easy.def: The people who live in one place.
examples: Our community has a park and a school.
People in our community help each other.
The community garden grows beans.

more.def: A group of people who live in the same area or who share something important.
examples: The whole community helped clean up the beach.
The school is an important part of our community.
A community of ants works together to build a nest.

easy.def: To look at two things to see how they are the same or not the same.
examples: Compare the two apples. Which is bigger?
We compare our hands to see whose is bigger.
Compare the two pictures.

more.def: To look closely at two or more things to find how they are alike and different.
examples: We compared the two maps and noticed that one had more rivers.
She compared prices at two stores before buying the shoes.
In science, we compared how fast ice melts in sun and shade.
It takes courage to try new things.
The knight had a lot of courage.
It took courage to pet the big dog.

more.def: The strength to do something even though it is scary or hard.
examples: It took courage to tell the truth about what happened.
The firefighters showed great courage during the rescue.
He found the courage to try out for the school play.
